items.answer: Give credit analysts two things: (1) a notch calculator helper that takes a previous and a current rating and returns the notch change, its direction and the resulting WL, and (2) the Indicator 12 (country rating change) WL rule. Both are pure ESM functions that other POC parts import. Success means the contract functions return the values set by REQ-06-02 and REQ-03-12 as corrected by C2/C3/C6, checked by `node --test`.

items.answer: End users are credit analysts. They use the functions through POC screens that other parts build later. The direct consumers in this slice are other POC modules that import the contract. No UI or access surface means no role-based permissions in this slice.

items.answer: IN: src/ratings/notch.mjs (RATING_SCALE, notchChange, notchCalculator) and src/indicators/countryRating.mjs (countryRatingChangeWl), plus their node:test tests. OUT: fetching ratings from a public source (C4); override parameter, persistence and audit trail (C7); UI, CLI and printed output (C8); Indicator 13 (REQ-03-13) as an indicator of its own (only its thresholds are reused by the calculator, C2); every other POC requirement.

items.answer: Downgrades and unchanged ratings have concrete examples. Calculator: BBB+→BB+ = 3-notch downgrade, WL 2; BBB+→BBB- = 2 notches, WL 1; a 1-notch downgrade gives WL 0. Indicator 12: 1 notch → WL 1, 2+ notches → WL 2. Upgrades and unchanged → WL 0 for both. One gap: no example fixes notchCalculator().notches for an upgrade (see CON-interface, open).
items.quote: so BBB+ → BB+ = 3-notch downgrade → WL=2, and BBB+ → BBB- = 2 notches → WL=1 … 1 notch → WL=1; 2+ notches → WL=2 … Upgrades and unchanged ratings → WL=0 for both indicators. … A 1-notch downgrade gives calculator WL 0

items.answer: The request resolves its own conflicts: (1) The REQ-06-02 example 'BBB+ → BB+ = 2 notch downgrade → WL=1' miscounts. C2 rules it is 3 notches, WL 2, and that the calculator uses the Indicator 13 thresholds. (2) Calculator 1 notch → WL 0 while Indicator 12 1 notch → WL 1; C6 rules both stand. (3) 'Pre-filled from public source' is out of scope; the rating is an input (C4). (4) 'auto-filled value editable' is met because the caller passes the confirmed or edited rating (C7). (5) 'displayed' is met by the returned object (C8). The missing C5 leaves a gap, not a contradiction; it is tracked under CON-interface (open).

items.question: What sign does notchCalculator(previous, current).notches carry for an upgrade? The request fixes the sign only for notchChange ('positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged'). For notchCalculator it says only `{ notches, direction, wl }`. C2 speaks of a '3-notch downgrade', which is a size plus a direction word. The clarification that settled this (C5) is missing. Downgrades (e.g. BBB+→BB+ = 3) and unchanged (0) come out the same either way; only upgrades differ.
options: A — signed, same as notchChange: notches = notchChange(previous, current); AA→AAA gives { notches: -1, direction: 'upgrade', wl: 0 }; BBB→BBB+ gives { notches: -1, ... }
B — unsigned size, direction carries the sign: notches = |notchChange|; AA→AAA gives { notches: 1, direction: 'upgrade', wl: 0 }
items.impact: This is a public contract other POC parts import, and the POC screens will show this value as 'notch change' (C8). A shows '-1 upgrade'; B shows '1 upgrade'. Dev unit tests and QA expectations for every upgrade case depend on it. Changing it after other parts integrate breaks them.

Any input to notchChange, notchCalculator or countryRatingChangeWl that, after trimming and case-folding, is not one of the 19 C1 ratings throws a RangeError, for either argument. Examples that throw: '' (empty), '   ', 'BBB +', 'BBB−' (non-ASCII minus), 'CC', 'C', 'D', 'SD', 'NR', 'Baa1'. Nothing is caught or replaced with a fallback; no WL is returned for invalid input. Still open: which whitespace counts as trimmed (X-input-whitespace), the error type for non-string input (X-input-nonstring), and the message text (X-error-message, pm).

items.answer: notchChange(previous, current) returns the integer index(current) − index(previous) on RATING_SCALE (best first). Positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged. Range −18..+18. Examples: ('BBB+','BB+') → 3; ('BBB+','BBB-') → 2; ('AA','AAA') → −1; ('A','A') → 0; ('AAA','CCC-') → 18; ('CCC-','AAA') → −18.
items.quote: A notch is one step on this scale. … `notchChange(previous, current)` → integer; positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged.

items.answer: notchCalculator returns { notches, direction, wl }. direction is 'downgrade' when notchChange > 0, 'upgrade' when < 0, 'unchanged' when 0 (lower-case strings, exactly these three). The meaning of notches for upgrades is open (CON-interface).
items.quote: `notchCalculator(previous, current)` → `{ notches, direction: "downgrade" | "upgrade" | "unchanged", wl }`

items.answer: notchCalculator wl (number): downgrade of 1 notch → 0; 2 notches → 1; 3 or more → 2 (maximum 2, e.g. AAA→CCC- → 2). Upgrade or unchanged → 0. Examples: BBB+→BBB → 0; BBB+→BBB- → 1; BBB+→BB+ → 2; BB+→BBB+ → 0; A→A → 0.
items.quote: The calculator's WL uses the Indicator 13 thresholds (2 notches → WL=1, 3+ → WL=2) … Upgrades and unchanged ratings → WL=0 for both indicators. … A 1-notch downgrade gives calculator WL 0

items.answer: countryRatingChangeWl(previous, current) returns the number 0, 1 or 2 and is computed from notchChange. Downgrade of 1 notch → 1; 2 or more → 2. Upgrade or unchanged → 0. Examples: BBB+→BBB → 1; BBB+→BBB- → 2; BBB+→BB+ → 2; AAA→CCC- → 2; BBB→BBB+ → 0; BBB→BBB → 0. Invalid input throws RangeError (CON-errors).
items.quote: 1 notch → WL=1; 2+ notches → WL=2 … Upgrades and unchanged ratings → WL=0 for both indicators. … `countryRatingChangeWl(previous, current)` → 0 | 1 | 2 (REQ-03-12 thresholds, C3), built on `notchChange`

items.answer: RATING_SCALE lists exactly these 19 upper-case ASCII strings, best first: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-. Index 0 = 'AAA', index 18 = 'CCC-'. Ratings outside it (CC, C, SD, D, NR, Moody's notation) are not on the scale and are rejected (CON-errors).
items.quote: Rating scale, best to worst (19 steps): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-. … `RATING_SCALE` — the 19 ratings of C1, best first.

items.question: C1 says input is 'trimmed' but does not say which characters are trimmed. Which leading and trailing characters are removed before matching?
options: A — JavaScript String.prototype.trim(): all Unicode whitespace and line terminators (space, tab, \n, \r, NBSP U+00A0, U+2003 …). ' bbb+\n' and '\u00A0BBB+' are accepted.
B — ASCII space only (U+0020). '\tBBB+' and '\u00A0BBB+' throw RangeError.
C — ASCII whitespace only (space, \t, \n, \r, \f, \v). '\u00A0BBB+' throws RangeError.
items.impact: Decides whether inputs pasted from a public source or spreadsheet (tabs, NBSP, newlines) are accepted or rejected with a RangeError. Observable behaviour of all three functions; QA test data depends on it. Inner whitespace ('BBB +') is rejected under every option.

items.question: What happens when an argument is not a string (null, undefined, a number, an object, or a missing argument)? C1 says 'anything else is rejected with a RangeError', but its subject is text input that is trimmed and case-folded. A non-string cannot be trimmed, and JavaScript convention throws TypeError for a wrong type.
options: A — RangeError for every invalid input, including null, undefined, 123 and {} (literal reading of C1: one error type for consumers to catch)
B — TypeError for non-string input; RangeError only for strings that are not a C1 rating
C — String-coerce first (String(x)) and then validate, so null becomes 'null' and throws RangeError
items.impact: The thrown error type is part of the public contract that callers catch. Consumers that check `instanceof RangeError` would miss a TypeError. Affects the tests of all three functions.
